portInfo.description: Málaga is a walkable Costa del Sol cruise call for many ships berthing near Muelle Uno and the central passenger terminals. The Alcazaba, cathedral, and Picasso Museum sit within a short taxi or energetic walk, with day trips to Granada possible on longer calls.
portInfo.location: Andalusia, southern Spain, on the Costa del Sol
portInfo.language: Spanish; English widely spoken in tourism

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Most cruise berths are on the downtown waterfront near the cruise terminal / Muelle Uno promenade—confirm the exact gate on ship signage.
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Often under 1–2 km to the historic center from central berths
gettingThere.walkingTime: Frequently 10–25 minutes to cathedral / Atarazanas area from central piers—confirm on your sailing programme before you rely on a fixed walk time.
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Short taxi hops help for Gibralfaro or travelers avoiding hills/heat
gettingThere.publicTransport: Local buses cover hill neighborhoods. Granada is a longer rail/coach excursion—not a casual add-on to a short Málaga walk.
gettingThere.distanceAnswer: Often under 1–2 km to the historic center from central berths

thingsToDo.intro: Málaga is often a walkable Costa del Sol call from central berths near Muelle Uno. Granada is a separate full-day excursion—not a casual add-on.
topThings: Palmeral de las Sorpresas / port-city waterfront
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Midday Alcazaba climbs are hot. If Granada is on your list, assume it consumes the day—do not also plan a full Málaga museum crawl.
